recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Only revisit if a future WG decision says List itself should implement the Participant pattern; otherwise adding List or duplicate prose would conflict with the seed comments or risk maintenance drift.
issue_request: FHIR-27822 asked to fix required PlanDefinition.action.participant.type because it lacked non-clinical participant choices such as List and Organization; the Published/Persuasive R5 resolution was to expand participant types to resources implementing the Participant pattern.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-27822. R5-era participant-model commits c68fb1d080 and f83e1f04c1 changed the same PlanDefinition source by making action.participant.type optional, adding actor modeling, and expanding action-participant-type to the Participant-pattern code set including Organization and Group.
additional_context: Jira comments record that List cannot be a Participant and that Group may satisfy collection use cases. Current fhir.ini includes the Participant logical patterns and PlanDefinition in build scope. Later participant decisions added reference/canonical targets for definitional and non-clinical use cases, including Medication, Specimen, Substance/BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and SubstanceDefinition, without changing the Participant-pattern code set to include List.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already resolves the original required-code limitation through optional type plus typeCanonical/typeReference choices; action-participant-type matches current Participant-pattern resources and List remains intentionally excluded.

related_jiras.note: PlanDefinition actor/function modeling changed action.participant.type from required to optional and shaped the current participant model.
Added definitional participant targets, supporting the current typeCanonical/typeReference approach.
Later PlanDefinition participant issue rejected ResearchSubject as a participant but added other allowable typeReference participants, reinforcing the choice-based model.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive issue requesting PlanDefinition.action.participant.type support for non-clinical participants, resolved to use resources implementing the Participant pattern.
evidence_items.learned: The final WG decision is to align with Participant-pattern resources; comments explain that List itself is not a Participant and Group was the likely collection representation.

evidence_items.summary: fhir.ini lists participant, participantcontactable, and participantliving as logical patterns and PlanDefinition as an active resource.

evidence_items.summary: PlanDefinition.action.participant.type is optional and is followed by typeCanonical and typeReference participant choices.
